notes.meaning: Simeon's clan received the second share of land drawn at Shiloh, and it was placed right inside the borders of Judah. Jacob had long ago warned that Simeon's descendants would be scattered because of their father's past violence. Unlike other tribes that had a whole separate region to themselves, Simeon lived among Judah's towns.

These verses name the first group of towns given to Simeon in the dry southern area known as the Negev. Beersheba is famous as a place where Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob dug wells and worshiped God. Hormah was an important site where Israel won a key victory during their desert travels.

This list finishes the first group of thirteen towns given to Simeon. Ziklag later became famous as the town where David stayed while hiding from King Saul. These towns had small farming villages clustered around them for extra support and protection.

Simeon also received four other towns and their surrounding settlements, reaching as far south as Baalath-beer. Two of these towns sat in the southern desert and two lay in the low foothills to the west. Because these towns were spread out in different parts of Judah's land, Simeon lived scattered rather than in one solid territory.

The land surveyors realized that Judah had originally been given far more land than its people needed. Judah graciously shared their extra land without complaining so their brothers in Simeon would have a home. God guided this practical adjustment to meet everyone's needs fairly.

The third lot was drawn for the tribe of Zebulun, beginning at the town of Sarid. Zebulun received its lot before older brother Issachar, matching the order Jacob and Moses had given in their ancient blessings. Their new home sat in a rich and fertile valley in the north.

The border of Zebulun stretched westward toward the Mediterranean Sea, passing Maralah and reaching the stream near Jokneam. Even though other tribes touched the coast directly, Zebulun's borders reached close enough to benefit from ocean trade. This matched Jacob's prophecy that Zebulun would enjoy the blessings of the sea.

Looking east from Sarid, the boundary ran along the slopes of Mount Tabor toward Daberath and up to Japhia. These towns marked the line between Zebulun and their neighboring brothers to the south and east. Daberath later became a town set aside for the Levites to live in.

From there, the border continued eastward toward Gath-hepher, Eth-kazin, and Rimmon, before turning toward Neah. Gath-hepher is best known in the Bible as the hometown of the prophet Jonah. Rimmon was another town that would later be given to the Levites.
The northern line of Zebulun circled around toward Hannathon and ended at the Valley of Iphtah-el. This deep valley formed a natural northern boundary between Zebulun and the tribe of Asher.

Zebulun received twelve major cities along with their country villages, including Shimron and Bethlehem. This Bethlehem was in northern Israel, not the town in Judah where King David and Jesus were born. These settlements formed the complete homeland for the families of Zebulun.

The fourth lot came out for the tribe of Issachar. Their land was mostly described by a list of cities rather than boundary lines, because it was framed by the surrounding tribes. It sat in the great, fertile plain of Jezreel between Zebulun to the north and Manasseh to the south.

Issachar's inheritance included well-known towns such as Jezreel and Shunem. Jezreel later became the royal winter home of King Ahab, while Shunem was the hometown of the woman who kindly gave shelter to the prophet Elisha. These towns lay in one of the richest farming areas in all of Canaan.

This list names seven more towns belonging to Issachar, including Kishion and En-gannim. Both of these towns were later set apart for the Levites who served God in Israel. The name En-gannim means 'spring of gardens,' pointing to the fruitful orchards and flowing waters of the district.

Issachar's border reached Mount Tabor and went eastward all the way to the Jordan River. In total, Issachar held sixteen cities with their outlying farming villages. The tribe was blessed with flat, productive soil and good access to fresh water.
The fifth lot was drawn for the tribe of Asher, the descendants of Jacob's son by Zilpah. Their territory stretched along the western sea coast of Canaan, north of Mount Carmel.

Asher's southern territory included cities like Helkath and reached down to Mount Carmel by the sea. Carmel was famous for its rich soil, thick trees, and lush beauty, fulfilling Jacob's blessing that Asher would enjoy rich food. Helkath and Mishal were later assigned to the Levites as dwelling places.
